title: SCIM sequencing and retry orchestration for group membership consistency
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: SCIM provisioning events for users and groups (create/update/delete/membership changes) sometimes arrive out-of-order or are retried by identity providers, causing transient inconsistencies in group -> RBAC role assignments. These inconsistencies can lead to brief over-privilege or orphaned access for users. This ticket designs and implements a deterministic sequencing and retry orchestration layer to ensure membership changes are applied idempotently and in an order-safe way, with durable retries, telemetry, and operator controls.
design_summary: 1) Per-entity SCIM sequence anchor: attach a monotonically increasing sequence token to each processed event (source-provided if available, otherwise our sequence by timestamp+nonce). 2) Staging + apply phase: write incoming change to a 'pending_scim' table with request_id, seq_token, org_id, actor, raw_payload, expiry/tombstone. Only advance authoritative membership state when seq_token is >= last_applied. 3) Idempotency keys: honor identity provider 'If-Match' / external id mapping and store request_id for dedupe. 4) Retry orchestration: transient errors trigger async retry queue with exponential backoff + jitter; 5xx/timeout -> local retry; 4xx auth/permission -> mark connector invalid and alert; 409/conflict -> re-evaluate sequence and replay. 4) Reconciliation job (delta-worker) runs per-org daily and on-demand to reconcile group deltas and repair missed ops. 5) Audit logging: every transition (pending->applied->tombstone) emits structured audit event with before/after snapshot and request metadata.
tradeoffs_and_alternatives: We considered strict linear sequence enforcement by blocking apply until we see all adjacent sequence numbers; rejected because it stalls applies under dropped events from providers. Alternative is optimistic apply with reconciliation which we chose for availability. Durable queue increases complexity and storage but provides stronger guarantees for delivery vs simple in-memory retries. We avoid cross-org global locks to keep throughput; instead we use per-org/per-entity locks.
acceptance_criteria:
- New SCIM events applied with idempotency: duplicate request_ids do not change state.
- No more than 0.1% of membership updates result in orphaned role assignments in canary orgs after 48h.
- Retry queue depth should be <= 50 for normal load; spikes require alerting.
- Reconciliation job must correct 99% of detected deltas within one run.
- Structured audit events emitted for every applied/deprovision action and ingested by audit-logs pipeline.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (week 1): Add pending_scim table, wire incoming SCIM handler to write staging row and return 202. Phase 2 (week 2): Implement apply worker that reads pending rows ordered by seq_token and performs idempotent apply to memberships and RBAC mapping. Phase 3 (week 3): Retry queue + backoff, circuit breaker for invalid connectors, integrant tests with Okta/OneLogin mocks. Phase 4 (week 4): Reconciliation job + dashboards + canary rollout. Phase 5: Full rollout after 2-week canary and metrics validation.
observability_and_alerting: Metrics to add: scim.incoming.rate, scim.apply.latency.p50/p95, scim.apply.errors.count, scim.retry_queue.depth, scim.reconciliation.fixes.count, scim.tombstone.count. Dashboards: Grafana board 'SCIM Provisioning - RBAC' with per-region/per-org drilldown. Alerts: pager when retry_queue.depth > 500 for >10m, or connector_auth_failures > 10/min. Sentry breadcrumb for per-request errors and span tracing via X-Request-ID.
test_plan: Unit tests for sequence comparison and idempotency logic. Integration tests against Okta/OneLogin test harness: reorder events, duplicate events, missing events. Chaos test: inject 25% event reorder and measure reconciliation corrections. Load test: simulate 10k user updates/hour across 100 orgs and verify retry queue behavior and latency SLOs.
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind 'scim_sequence_orchestration'. Canary: onboard 5 low-risk enterprise customers for 48h; monitor metrics and audit logs. If stable, roll to 30% orgs for one week, then 100% with continued monitoring. Provide quick rollback toggle that disables apply worker and lets pending rows expire to avoid accidental mass deprovisioning.
security_and_compliance: All SCIM payloads are encrypted at rest; access to pending_scim rows is RBAC-protected. Audit logs include actor and IP and are forwarded to the central audit pipeline (retention policy per compliance team). The change requires a security review (see security_review_required). We add an HMAC signature verification step for signed SCIM connectors where available.
open_questions:
- Should we trust provider-provided sequence tokens (e.g., Okta event IDs) as canonical when present, or always normalize? Decision: prefer provider tokens but fall back to internal sequence for unsigned sources.
- How long to keep tombstones before hard-delete? Proposal: 90 days for reconciliation safety.
- Should reconciliation include application-level timestamps for RBAC role expiration? We will add expiry metadata if requested by Product.
